# /crav1-plan-from-spec

[All skills](../skills.md) · Walkthrough: [From a spec to a plan](../../from-spec-to-plan.md) · Playbook: [`SKILL.md`](../../../.cursor/skills/crav1/crav1-plan-from-spec/SKILL.md)

## Purpose

Turn an accepted spec into a file-level plan.md and independently testable tasks.md.

File-level `plan.md` and `tasks.md`; each verify note names the checks before code; names a linter or checker when the repo has one, and stops before Build when it does not; refuses to code and does not install a linter. When the spec is partial or `## In the code` names paths, reads that repo and branch and chooses finish the gap, add a verify test, or leave it before any task. A piece that already matches v0 is not a choice.

1.64.0: Built pieces reads every work branch of the spec without checkout (and `../<repo>` for another repo), labels pieces `only on <branch>, not merged`, and ends a task with `(branch: …)` when its piece lives on one branch.

1.68.0: a task may name a sub-branch of the spec branch, `(branch: feat/orders-capacity-t3)`.

1.87.0: each kept-open question that does not block the demo becomes its own entry under `## Risks`, without asking whether to park or answer it.

1.125.0: once `tasks.md` exists, a leftover that blocks some current tasks gets `Blocks: T#` and the risk line says do not implement until resolved. A leftover that blocks no current task gets `Blocks: none`, and that risk line does not say do not implement until resolved. When current or later is unclear, one short batch asks. No `Blocks:` line still means the whole slice.

1.126.0: a question with `Blocks: T2, T4` gets the risk line `kept open; blocks T2, T4 until resolved.` Only a question with no `Blocks:` line keeps do not implement until resolved. A risk matches on the question first sentence or a `(question: <first words>)` tag, not the whole line.

1.128.0: optional `(step: 1)` links a task to a numbered Approach step, and optional `(map: feat/cancel-refund)` puts that task on another branch. Leave both off. The default build map is one branch per step.

## Runs when

Spec is accepted. Called by the user.

## Prompts

The gate may ask one architecture batch. Leftovers that might be current work or later work are one short batch, current or later, not one question at a time. The closing yes is the third. Skip a batch that does not apply. A value the user left out is outside the budget. A prompt may hold several questions. See the asking rule in `crav1.mdc`.

## Reads

In short: Spec, diagrams, ADRs; the named repo and branch when the slice is partial.

Reads the accepted spec, diagrams, ADRs, exports, kept security findings already written, and, when the spec is partial or `## In the code` names paths, that same committed repo and branch before any task is written.

## Writes

In short: `plan.md`, `tasks.md`, `Blocks:` or `Blocks: none` on kept-open questions, and matching OpenSpec export files when those already exist.

Writes `plan.md` and `tasks.md`, and matching OpenSpec export files when those already exist. A built piece that already matches v0 is marked already there and gets no rebuild task. A piece the user leaves gets one line in the plan and no task. Lists each kept-open question under Risks without asking whether to park it, and stale research findings under Risks. That does not block the plan. Writes `Blocks: T#` or `Blocks: none` under a kept-open question. A `Blocks: T#` risk says kept open; blocks those tasks until resolved. A `Blocks: none` risk says kept open; does not block the current tasks. Only a question with no `Blocks:` line keeps do not implement until resolved.

## Does not

Leaves `spec.md` alone except a `Blocks:` line under a kept-open question. Leaves application code and any linter install alone.

Limits and exceptions: when `## Linter` says this repo has no linter for the code the tasks will touch, it stops before Build until the user chooses. A line under `## Dismissed test suggestions` is not a task. A kept test suggestion that is already an acceptance line maps to a task. A gap or a disagreement is finish, add a verify test, or leave before any task exists. A later run does not turn a left piece into work unless the user says so. Stale research does not fail the gate.
